description: FieldShift Explorers is a student-led team using NASA data and satellite observations to explore smarter farming solutions, especially for rural India. We welcome learners interested in space science, agriculture, AI, programming, and data analysis. Together, we aim to turn scientific data into practical insights through innovation, teamwork, and creativity.
summary: FieldShift transforms NASA Earth observation data into simple, local agricultural climate information for the Shirdi–Kopargaon region of Maharashtra, India. It uses NASA POWER historical weather data to analyse temperature, rainfall and solar radiation. The project includes data-quality checks, climate indicators and a dashboard to help users understand local climate patterns. Open-Meteo forecasts are shown separately from historical NASA observations. FieldShift aims to support farmers, students and local planners in exploring climate-related agricultural challenges and adaptation possibilities.
details:
FieldShift is a prototype climate-information dashboard for the Shirdi–Kopargaon region of Maharashtra.

It retrieves historical daily climate data from NASA POWER and processes temperature, precipitation and solar radiation. The system checks missing dates and duplicate records and calculates climate indicators such as dry days and high-temperature screening days.

The analysed information is presented through a dashboard and downloadable reports. Open-Meteo forecast information is integrated separately to help users view upcoming weather conditions.

The project analysed 667 valid observations, with a mean temperature of 25.71°C and total recorded precipitation of 1609.6 mm. These are historical dataset statistics, not farm-level measurements.

The project is designed to make Earth observation data easier to understand and explore. It is an early decision-support prototype, not a validated crop recommendation system. Future work includes soil information, crop-specific analysis and field testing.
